newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wrightson says profit to be below forecast.
newsitem.headline: Wrightson says profit to be below forecast.

text.p: Rural servicing company Wrightson Ltd said on Friday that trading performance was being affected by a deepening rural downturn.
"Indications at this stage are that the half and full year results will be significantly below the forecast profit range," it told the Stock Exchange in response to an inquiry about its share price.
"In our view, it is the rural downturn and the expected consequential impact of this on the company's trading performance that the market is reacting to."
Wrightson's shares have fallen to $1.05 from $1.27 on December 1.
In November, the Wrightson Chairman, Sir Ronald Trotter, told shareholders that "the first 3 months had been below expectations".

He went on to say that, while it was too early to be precise, the board's expectation at that stage was that the forecast profit range of $24 milion to $27 million would be achieved albeit at the lower end.

Since that time, Wrightson said the rural downturn had deepened, particularly in the sheep and cattle sectors where Wrightson does most of its business, and the company's trading performance has, as a consequence, been adversely impacted, a situation which is expected to continue for as long as conditions remain unchanged in the rural sector.
The re-organisation of the company announced last year, had also had some negative impact on aspects of the business, Wrightson said.
The company is currently preparing its half year accounts which will be released in early March.
